also: put it on the rack to cool

terms.gloss: a small grating, a gridiron: a cooling rack
evidence: Mart. 14.221.1: rāra tibi curvā crāticula sūdet ofellā
terms.comment: Classically a small gridiron set over the fire (Lewis & Short: “fine hurdle-work; hence, a small gridiron”; see “grill”). Its use for the wire rack a cake cools on is modern, and ours: we have found no word for a cooling rack in Traupman, Morgan–Owens, or Levi–Bini. Columella’s cheeses were set to dry on racks made for the purpose, crātēs, spaced so that none touched another; see the examples.

evidence: Col. 7.8.5: sub umbrā crātibus in hoc factīs

phrases.latin: Placentam in crāticulā pōne, ut refrīgēscat.
phrases.english: Put the cake on the cooling rack to cool.

phrases.latin: Crustula in crāticulā refrīgēscant; nōlī adhūc tangere.
phrases.english: Let the biscuits cool on the rack; don’t touch them yet.

phrases.latin: aquā dulcī abluitur et sub umbrā crātibus in hoc factīs ita ōrdinātur, nē alter alterum cāseus contingat et ut modicē siccētur
phrases.english: it is washed in fresh water and laid out in the shade on racks made for the purpose, so that no cheese touches another and each dries a little
